### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/formula`, `@objectstack/objectql`, touching **45** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/formula/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**26** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a485b5a3e28d84550e8a33bbb5cfc2d52c82ff9e`.

⛔ **10** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/formula/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `ObjectQL (symbol, 72 pages)`
- **5** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **55** of **207** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **25** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a485b5a3e28d84550e8a33bbb5cfc2d52c82ff9e` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `37d5eb6037c6db34d5546c8cb6ff68412747c005` — the merge of head `8ffe3ae67856cc968eb7ae61788f1b2f6611cac3` into base `a485b5a3e28d84550e8a33bbb5cfc2d52c82ff9e`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 37d5eb6037c6db34d5546c8cb6ff68412747c005 && git checkout 37d5eb6037c6db34d5546c8cb6ff68412747c005
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin a485b5a3e28d84550e8a33bbb5cfc2d52c82ff9e 8ffe3ae67856cc968eb7ae61788f1b2f6611cac3 && git checkout -B drift-repro a485b5a3e28d84550e8a33bbb5cfc2d52c82ff9e && git merge --no-ff 8ffe3ae67856cc968eb7ae61788f1b2f6611cac3

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a485b5a3e28d84550e8a33bbb5cfc2d52c82ff9e
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs a485b5a3e28d84550e8a33bbb5cfc2d52c82ff9e` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `f780ce7816bc82896e4777be152ee6e4e4ec6455`
Local-runs: none
Scope: skills/objectstack-formula/SKILL.md + packages/formula/src/stdlib.ts, packages/formula/src/types.ts, packages/formula/src/validate.ts, packages/formula/src/cel-engine.ts, packages/formula/src/index.ts, packages/objectql/src/formula-option-labels.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine.ts (the `applyFormulaPlan` / `hydrateWriteFormulas` / `computeStoredExpressions` / `evaluateFormulaField` / `serveFormulaField` / `find` / `findOne` / `insert` / `update` hunks), .changeset/26608-formula-option-label.md, content/docs/data-modeling/formulas.mdx (cited, read against the code; the test files and the dogfood test were read to judge them, not reviewed)

Inputs read: card #26608 (body, triage 6440185938, claim 6442789358, amendment 6442958772, os-dev-report 6444975664), PR #26755 body and file list, the net diff `43731031..f780ce78` (merge-base of `origin/main`), and the check-runs on the head. The PR has no reviews and one bot comment (docs-drift, advisory). The head's tree was read through a detached `git checkout` of the fetched sha for file reads only — nothing built, run or re-run — and the checkout was restored afterwards.

### ① Derived judgments

Each accept-set or public-surface change the diff implies, named right or wrong against the tree:

1. **CEL grammar widens by one bare-callable name, `label`, registered as a MACRO** (`stdlib.ts` `bindOptionLabel`, `env.registerFunction('label(ast): string', …)`). The type check accepts exactly the AST shape `record.FIELD` (`optionLabelFieldOf`: op `.`, receiver `id` = `record`, non-empty string member) and refuses a literal, a path through a lookup, an optional read, `previous.FIELD` and a computed argument with one message (`LABEL_ARGUMENT_REFUSAL`). Registered unconditionally, like `can` and `hasCapability`, so the publish gate's answer does not depend on which context built the environment. **Right.** The widening reaches every CEL surface the skill lists (formula, `visibleWhen`, validation `when`, hook/sharing `condition`, flow, seed) because the stdlib is one environment; only the engine's formula serving pins `optionLabels`, so everywhere else `label()` compiles and then faults at run time (see ④).
2. **`EvalContext.optionLabels` (type `EvalOptionLabels`, field → stored value as text → label) is pure data, not a CEL variable.** `buildScope` (`stdlib.ts` ~764-787) mounts `record`, `previous`, `input`, `user`/`os`, `org`, `env`, `extra` only; `optionLabels` travels on `StdLibBinding` and is read through `read()` at call time, as the permission binding is. `stdlib.ts` imports no translator, no i18n type, no resolver. **Right**, and it is the seat instruction's first invariant.
3. **`@objectstack/formula` public surface**: `EvalOptionLabels` exported from `index.ts`; `registerStdLib` gains a fourth optional parameter (`index.ts` already exported it); `CEL_STDLIB_FUNCTIONS` gains `'label'`. All additive. **Right.**
4. **Catalog counts in `validate.ts`** (77 registered / 42 bare / 35 receiver-only / 30 from `registerStdLib` / 38 advertised): the advertised list moved 37 → 38 and the bare count 41 → 42 by exactly the one name the diff registers; `cel-stdlib-drift.test.ts` asserts list identities (`toEqual([])`, the withheld set), not the prose numbers, so the `hasCapability` absorption the dev reports (34 → 35 receiver-only) is a prose repair of a count main already under-stated. **Right**; Test Core will measure it.
5. **`@objectstack/objectql` surface**: `setI18nService` accepts three more optional methods (`getTranslations`, `getFallbackLocale`, `getDefaultLocale`), which `II18nService` already carries and `plugin.ts:1167` already passes whole. Additive. **Right.**
6. **`evaluateFormulaField` (exported, sync) changes behaviour**: a `label()` formula no longer faults with "no option labels" but evaluates against `declaredOptionLabels(schema, plan)`. Disclosed in its docblock and in the PR's reader table. **Right** as a documented exception (judged in ④).
7. **One translation path.** `readerOptionLabels` builds the bundle as `metaTranslationBundleOf` does (`getLocales()` × `getTranslations(locale)`, `meta-item-read-gate.ts:2757-2769`), builds the options as `metaTranslateOptions` does (`fallbackChain: [getFallbackLocale()]`, `defaultLocale: getDefaultLocale()`, `:2783-2790`), and calls the same `translateObject` from `@objectstack/spec/system` with `{ name, fields }`. `translateObject` (`i18n-resolver.ts:3837`) resolves a field's option label as `objects.NAME.fields.FIELD.options.VALUE` then `picklists.PICKLIST.options.VALUE` (`:3878-3889`) when the field carries `picklist`; `optionFields` keeps the whole field def so the `picklist` key survives, and every registry read passes `finishServedObject` → `resolvePicklistFields` (`registry.ts:3838-3855`), so a picklist-bound field reaches the module with its options resolved. No key is spelled in objectql. **Right**, and the dogfood test pins `/meta/object` label == formula label on one boot.
8. **Locale**: `ExecutionContext.locale`, which both the REST and the MCP door set from `Accept-Language` (`resolve-execution-context.ts:216`, `preferredLocaleFromHeader`, the same parser `metaRequestLocale` uses). **Right** for every request that sends the header (the console always does). Observation, not a finding: with no header, the metadata route falls to `?locale=` then `getDefaultLocale()`, while the execution context falls to the settings service's localization — the two can disagree only on a header-less request, and the dogfood "no locale" case is served the declared labels, which is the documented answer.
9. **Readers wired (the claim names them; each one found in the tree)**: `find` (`engine.ts:13590-13596`), `findOne` (`:13879-13883`), the insert 201 body (`hydrateWriteFormulas`, `:15855-15861`), the by-id update body (`:17800-17807`; a predicate update returns a count and has no rows to hydrate, pre-existing), `serveFormulaField` (`:6594-6597`, and `ScopedContext.serveFormulaField` at `:22003` passes the hook's own execution context), `expand` (`expandRelatedRecords` runs `this.find` with `{ ...execCtx, __expandRead: true }`, so a lookup's display name follows the reader). Stored expressions: both `storedExpressionServing` objects (insert `:14960`, update `:16364`) carry `optionLabelsFor: declaredOptionLabels`, and all four `computeStoredExpressions` sites share them. No REST export or MCP path evaluates formulas on its own: every one found goes through `engine.find`/`findOne`. **Right; no reader missed.**
10. **Search**: a formula field has no column (the skill's own "formula is virtual" warning; `where`/`searchableFields` refuse one). Unchanged. **Right.**
11. **Tenant / permission**: the map is built from the read object's own declared `options` after that object's read doors; nothing from another object is reachable (the macro refuses `record.lookup.field` at compile; an `expand` is a separate `find` under the related object's doors). A reader allowed the formula but denied the select field reads the label of a value the formula already exposed raw before this PR — pre-existing, not widened. **No new leak.**

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/26608-formula-option-label.md`: `@objectstack/formula: minor`, `@objectstack/objectql: minor`, with `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: added` line-initial in both the changeset body and the PR body. A new accepted CEL function in an authorable `expression.source` is a new accepted value (`added`), and `added` on a package the diff moves takes at least `minor` (AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3): **matches**. Nothing is narrowed, removed or re-meant, so no BREAKING banner and no ADR-0087 disposition is owed. `@objectstack/dogfood` is `private: true`; `content/docs/**` is not a package. `skip-changeset` does not apply. **Right.**

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev flag: Tier H** (`skills/**` on the file list). Confirmed: landing waits for the maintainer's word; the Governed Surface Queue Guard is green on this head. This record is the contract-tier review of the governed paths; it does not substitute for the approval.
- **Dev flag: `Skills-docs: follow-up owed — skills/objectstack-formula/evals/cel-predicates-formulas.json`.** The form is the one the claim template allows (`.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/SKILL.md:313`: `follow-up owed — FILES`, which the seat rewrites to `#N` before ACCEPT after filing the card). SKILL.md and `formulas.mdx` teach `label()` in this diff; the eval does not exercise it. The file is at its ceiling (1046/1046 per the dev's ratchet reading; `check-skills-token-ratchet` is green). **Answered: deferral accepted; the seat files the owed card and rewrites the line.**
- **`open_questions[0]` — where does the `label()` eval land? Answer: A, a follow-up card.** Trimming evals 1–5 changes what those cases grade, which is a Tier H content decision for the maintainer (and the ceiling is a ratchet ruling, not a dev's call). The follow-up card should carry one compact `label(record.kind)` case plus the ceiling question, and — tied to ④ should-fix 1 — a negative case asserting `must_not_contain: ['label(']` in a validation-rule prompt, since that is the wrong authoring this surface now makes possible.
- **Dev flag: PR body not patched** (three cosmetic fixes the seat writes: the `需要你做的` section's second action moves to Acceptance notes, the bundle readings are missing, the Verification bullets are not folded). Prose outside `hits`; noted for the seat, not judged here.
- **Dev flag: `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` not measured locally**; the derived families on the head answer it (see the check-runs below).
- **Out-of-scope findings** (dev's): `label()` outside a formula faults at run time with no publish-time refusal — carried into ④; the dogfood `tsc` heap reading — environment, not a code finding.
- **Deviation from the order's sketch** (`EvalContext.locale` threaded into the function) to the accepted design (caller resolves data): recorded in amendment 6442958772 before the diff; the tree follows the amendment.

### ④ Design judgment

**`skills/objectstack-formula/SKILL.md`** (the `hits` file): a new "Options" table row for `label(record.f)`. Each claim was read against the code: "in the reader's locale" (engine reads: ①-8/9), "Only `record.FIELD`" (`optionLabelFieldOf`), "`''` for null" (`optionLabelOf`: `value === null || value === undefined` → `''`), "A stored (non-formula) field stores the declared label" (`storedExpressionServing.optionLabelsFor = declaredOptionLabels`, pinned by the objectql test's `search_name` case). The table header's promise ("every entry resolves at runtime, and this table documents them all") is enforced by `skill-catalog-sync.test.ts` and the drift probe, both updated. Token reading 5600/5997. **The row holds against the code and the card's scenario (a formula `nameField` composed of option labels, read on the toast, H1, related list and lookup).**

Attempts to break it, with the outcome of each:

- **`label()` reads only pinned data; `stdlib.ts` takes no resolver.** Holds (①-2). The map is read at call time through `read()`, so the shared evaluation environment answers each evaluation from its own map; the drift probe hands `optionLabels: { a: { 1: 'One' } }` and nothing else reads it.
- **A stored expression stores the declared label, never the writer's locale.** Holds: `declaredOptionLabels` ignores locale by construction; the objectql test writes under zh-CN and reads `search_name` = `v2 · Clean` off the store.
- **Value with no declared option → the stored value itself** (the select control shows the same). Silent by design and documented in the skill row's sibling docs; acceptable. **Null → `''`** (documented). **Multi-select → throws** `renders ONE option value` (`typeof value === 'object'`); the SQL driver's `formatOutput` `JSON.parse`s json columns on read (`sql-driver.ts:18724, :18858`), so a multi-select reaches the macro as an array and the fault is loud. **Unknown field → loud at publish** when a schema is in play (`buildEnv` registers `record` as the typed `OsRecordScope`, so `checker.check(args[0])` refuses an undeclared member) and, at run time, cel-js's `no_such_key` surfaces as a runtime fault. **Non-select field → see should-fix 1**: loud on a non-null value (`declares no options`), silent `''` on a null one, because the null check precedes the options check. **Context without `optionLabels` → throws**, which the engine never reaches (the map is built whenever `label(` is in the plan's sources); outside a formula field it is the loud fault the docs describe.
- **The sync `evaluateFormulaField` left out.** It evaluates with the DECLARED labels (not a throw, not the writer's locale). Its live readers: `resolveRecordTitle` (`record-title.ts:142`) when no serving channel is at hand, i.e. the hook sandbox's `ctx.recordTitle` fallback (`body-runner.ts:283`). `plugin-approvals` `recordTitleOf` reads the served row's column and is not on this path. So the only place a declared label is "served" is a hook that composes its own text from a title it evaluates without a read channel — the dev's disclosed exception; no console reader the card names reads it. **No wrong label is served to a named reader.** Noted as a seam for a later card if a hook consumer (notification text) surfaces.
- **Reader missed?** None found (①-9). A list view and a related list are `find`; an export or an MCP data tool reads through `find`/`findOne` with the door's execution context (`resolve-execution-context.ts:216` is the shared door for REST and `/mcp`).
- **Tenant/permission leak?** None new (①-11).
- **Map build cost**: `bundleOf` pulls every locale's bundle on each read whose plan calls `label(` — the same work `GET /meta/object` does per request; `planCallsOptionLabel` is one regex per formula source otherwise. Acceptable; an observation.

**Findings**

- **Should-fix 1 (skill row, the `hits` file).** The stdlib table is the one table the skill's predicate surfaces (`visibleWhen`, validation `when`, hook/sharing `condition`, flow) read from, and §"CEL surfaces" says an unevaluable validation predicate **aborts the write**. The row does not say that `label()` answers only where the engine serves a formula field; `formulas.mdx` does. An author who writes `label(record.status) == '草稿'` in a validation rule passes `os build` and then every write to that object faults. Add the clause to the row (≈15 tokens; 397 of headroom), e.g. "formula fields only — in a predicate it faults; compare the stored value there". Not a must-fix: the failure is loud, names the function, and nothing silently wrong is served.
- **Should-fix 2 (`stdlib.ts` `optionLabelOf`, cited code).** Check the field's options entry before the null short-circuit, so `label(record.title)` on a text field faults on every row rather than only on rows where `title` is non-null; and, where `ExprSchemaHint.fieldTypes` is present at publish (`validate.ts` `typeSoundnessIssue`), refuse `label()` on a field whose spec type declares no options so the shape is caught at build like the other argument shapes are. Both are tightenings of a loud path, not corrections of a served value.
- **Must-fix: none.**

**Check-runs on `f780ce78` at render time**: every concluded derived family is green — Lint (ESLint, repo & tooling, docs & code guards, CI/release/engine, PM dispatch-gates, scoped ×3), Type Check (source gates, consumer gates, debt ledger), Check Changeset (latest run; one earlier run cancelled by the re-run), Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Spec property liveness, Dogfood Regression Gate, Build Docs, Check Documentation Links, Test UI, Build UI Deps, Build Core, Build & E2E UI, Test Core 1/8, 7/8 and 8/8. Still in progress at the last reading: Test Core 2/8–6/8, Type Check · workspace, Type Check UI. Their conclusions are the gate verdicts for those families; the Tier H landing already waits on green CI and the maintainer's word, so this record's verdict stands on the tree and the concluded families, and the seat re-reads the head's check-runs before the landing.

Reviewed-by: `session_01WGufzfhobWEgUUrjz4rrbh`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## 席位核对 · ACCEPT · `domain:spec` seat 1 (#6017) · session `session_01WGufzfhobWEgUUrjz4rrbh` · 2026-10-27T15:29Z

Head `8ffe3ae67856cc968eb7ae61788f1b2f6611cac3`. Card #26608, claim `6442789358` (surface amended by `6442958772`), dev report `6444975664`.

- **Contract review:** owed at CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER for the formula function catalog (`label()`) and `skills/objectstack-formula/SKILL.md`. PASS `6445230404` at `f780ce78`, with no must-fixes. The one commit since then, `8ffe3ae6`, lands both should-fixes only:
  - (a) The SKILL.md `label()` row now says it works in formula fields only, and that in a predicate (validation, visibility, hook) it faults, so authors compare the stored value there.
  - (b) `optionLabelOf` checks the field's options before the null short-circuit, so `label(record.textfield)` faults on every row. `option-label.test.ts` pins a null text field faulting.

  The diff from `f780ce78` to `8ffe3ae6` is 3 files, +15/−9.
- **Lane seat (rest of the diff, TIER_DEFAULT):**
  - objectql builds the label map per read through `translateObject` in `ExecutionContext.locale`. That is the one path `GET /meta/object` serves, with picklist inheritance intact.
  - The map is wired into find, findOne, the insert and update responses, `serveFormulaField` and expand.
  - Stored expressions store the declared label.
  - The dogfood test pins POST, PATCH, GET and list in zh-CN and en-US on a real boot.
  - No `ui/**` change.
  - Search is unchanged.
- **Not carried:** the optional publish-time refusal of `label()` on a non-options field (`validate.ts` `typeSoundnessIssue`). The run-time fault is loud on every row.
- **Skills-docs:** `#26760`, the eval follow-up. `cel-predicates-formulas.json` is at 1046 / 1046, and the card carries the negative predicate case.
- **Shape:** `Fixes #26608`, 14 files. `@objectstack/formula` and `@objectstack/objectql` are minor. `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: added`. `check-governed-merges --pr 26755`: 1 path is governed (`skills/**`), 948 changed lines.
- **Gates:** check-runs on this head are 43 success, 9 skipped and 0 red.
- **Landing:** Tier H. The maintainer approved and armed it at 2026-10-27T15:07Z. This seat arms nothing.
